content: {"summary":"The OOMKilled of ledger-service‑02 in April 2025 was due to a memory leak that caused the JVM heap to continuously expand, leading to GC thrashing and eventual out‑of‑memory termination.","likely_cause":"GC thrashing caused by a memory‑leak‑driven heap expansion","confidence":"high","claims":[{"text":"The leak caused the heap to grow until it filled the container, resulting in OOMKilled.","evidence_ids":["RB-001#2","INC-0034#1"],"quote":"Usually a symptom of a heap that is too small for the working set, or of a leak."},{"text":"The runbook advises restarting the pod after a heap summary, raising memory limits, and setting MaxRAMPercentage, then opening a leak ticket.","evidence_ids":["RB-001#9"],"quote":"restart the affected pod after taking a heap summary... raise the memory limit and keep -XX:MaxRAMPercentage=75"}],"next_checks":["Check GC logs (/var/log/ledger/gc.log) for old‑gen usage trends","Verify that a heap summary was captured before pod restart","Confirm that memory limits were increased and MaxRAMPercentage set","Open and track a leak ticket with the captured heap summary"]}
